speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I see you have knee pain after increasing your physical activity; where exactly is the pain located, and did you hear a pop when it started?

To help me assess this, please tell me if you have any swelling, bruising, or instability in the joint.

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the recent volleyball activity involving pivoting and the worsening pain, have you experienced any "locking" (inability to fully straighten the knee), giving way, or a visible deformity? Also, what specific movements trigger the most pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain is localized to the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella, which is the classic location for the pes anserine bursa. Did the pain begin immediately after your volleyball activity or did it develop more gradually over the next few days? Also, does pressing directly on that specific spot reproduce the sharp pain?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), currently managed with oral contraceptive pills. Social history: Has recently joined a volleyball team.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pes Anserine Bursitis.

Based on your recent increase in volleyball activity, the specific location of your pain (medial tibia below the kneecap), and the worsening nature of the symptoms, this is consistent with inflammation of the pes anserine bursa. I do not need to order further tests as the clinical presentation is classic for this condition.
